requirement: The system shall allow a guest to register with name, e-mail, phone number, password, role (DONOR or NGO) and base location.
Passwords shall be at least 10 characters and contain an upper-case letter, a lower-case letter, a digit and a symbol; common passwords shall be rejected.
Passwords shall be stored using password_hash() with Argon2id (or bcrypt cost 12); plaintext or reversibly encrypted passwords are prohibited.
Login shall verify credentials with password_verify() and return a generic error message that does not reveal whether the e-mail exists.
After 5 failed logins for the same e-mail or IP within 15 minutes, further attempts shall be blocked for 15 minutes (HTTP 429) and the event logged.
On successful login the session ID shall be regenerated (session_regenerate_id(true)) to prevent session fixation.
Logout shall destroy the server-side session, expire the session cookie and record a LOGOUT event.
A logged-in user shall be able to view and update their profile (name, phone, location) and change their password after re-entering the current password.
NGO registration shall additionally collect NGO name, registration number, address, location and a registration certificate (PDF/JPG/PNG); the NGO stays PENDING until an administrator verifies it.
A user shall be able to request a password reset through a time-limited, single-use token sent by e-mail.
Administrators shall be able to deactivate an account; deactivated users cannot log in.
The system shall support the roles DONOR, NGO and ADMIN; each user has exactly one role.
Every protected API endpoint shall verify that a valid session exists (else 401) and that the role is permitted (else 403).
Object-level checks shall ensure donors modify only their own donations and NGOs only their own requirements/requests; administrators may moderate.
NGOs with verification_status other than VERIFIED shall be unable to publish requirements or request donations.
The React application shall hide routes and controls not permitted for the current role, but the server shall remain the sole authority.
Direct URL/API access shall not bypass authorisation; forbidden or missing objects shall not leak information (return 404 for other users’ private objects where appropriate).

A donor shall be able to add a donation with item name, category, description, condition (NEW, LIKE_NEW, USABLE), quantity, unit, expiry date (mandatory for food), pickup address, location and at least one image.
On creation available_quantity shall equal original_quantity and status shall be AVAILABLE.
A donor shall be able to view a list of their donations with status, quantity remaining and pending requests, and a detail page for each.

A donor shall be able to update description, condition, image, pickup details and quantity of a donation that is AVAILABLE or PARTIALLY_ALLOCATED; original_quantity shall not be reduced below the quantity already allocated.
A donor shall be able to delete a donation; deletion is a soft delete (is_deleted = true) and is refused while accepted requests are awaiting pickup.
The system shall maintain available_quantity separately from original_quantity and never allow it to be negative or greater than original_quantity.
Perishable donations past their expiry date shall be automatically set to EXPIRED by a scheduled job and excluded from matching.
Donor phone number and pickup address shall be stored encrypted (Section 7.6) and shown only to the counter-party after a request is accepted.
A verified NGO shall be able to add a requirement: category, item name, target quantity, urgency (CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW), description and fulfilment deadline.
A verified NGO shall be able to view its requirements with progress (fulfilled / target) and status.
A verified NGO shall be able to update a requirement (quantity, urgency, deadline, description) provided target_quantity is not set below fulfilled_quantity.
A verified NGO shall be able to delete/cancel a requirement; cancellation is refused while donor-accepted pickups for it are pending.
A requirement shall become PARTIALLY_MET when fulfilled_quantity > 0 and FULFILLED when fulfilled_quantity ≥ target_quantity.
Requirements past their deadline shall be flagged as overdue but remain visible in history.
Verified NGOs shall be able to browse available donations in list and map views.
Filters shall include category, item-name keyword, condition, minimum quantity, maximum distance, expiry window and availability.
Results shall support sorting (nearest, newest, quantity) and pagination (default 12 per page).
Guests shall see a public map with approximate (rounded) donation positions and no personal or address data.
The last used category/filter shall be remembered through the preference cookie (Section 7.4).
A verified NGO shall be able to request a specific quantity of a donation, optionally linked to one of its open requirements.
The requested quantity shall be a positive integer not exceeding the donation’s current available_quantity.
An NGO shall not hold more than one active (REQUESTED/ACCEPTED/PICKUP_SCHEDULED) request for the same donation.
The donor shall be able to accept or reject each request; acceptance shall re-check availability under a row lock and, if valid, reduce available_quantity by the accepted amount.

Allocation shall execute in a single PostgreSQL transaction (READ COMMITTED with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, or SERIALIZABLE with retry) so concurrent accepts never oversell stock; the losing request receives HTTP 409.
A partially accepted donation (e.g. 6 of 10 blankets) shall remain listed as PARTIALLY_ALLOCATED with the remaining quantity available to other NGOs.
An NGO may cancel its request before collection; the allocated quantity shall be restored to the donation.
Request status transitions shall follow the state machine in Section 13.2; illegal transitions shall be rejected with HTTP 409.
Donation status shall be derived: AVAILABLE (nothing allocated), PARTIALLY_ALLOCATED, ALLOCATED (available_quantity = 0), COMPLETED (all allocations collected), CANCELLED, EXPIRED.
After acceptance, the NGO (or donor) shall propose a pickup date/time; when confirmed the status becomes PICKUP_SCHEDULED.
On entering PICKUP_SCHEDULED the system shall generate a 6-digit OTP with random_int() and e-mail/display it only to the NGO representative.
Only a keyed hash (HMAC-SHA-256 with server secret and request ID) of the OTP shall be stored; the raw OTP is never persisted.
At hand-over the donor shall enter the OTP told by the NGO representative; a correct value moves the request to COLLECTED and increments the requirement’s fulfilled_quantity.
An OTP shall expire 24 hours after the scheduled time and be locked after 5 wrong attempts; an NGO can request a fresh OTP.
Both parties shall confirm completion; the request then becomes COMPLETED and is retained as history.
An administrator may override an OTP-blocked hand-over; the override shall be logged with a reason.
Administrators shall view NGO applications and their documents, and approve, reject (with reason) or request more information.
Administrators shall view, search, activate/deactivate users.
Administrators shall add, edit, delete (if unused) and reorder item categories.
Administrators shall moderate donations and requirements (hide/cancel with reason) and monitor all requests.
The admin dashboard shall show totals (users, NGOs, donations, completed hand-overs), fulfilment rate, category distribution and monthly trend charts.
Administrators shall view, filter and export session/audit logs (Section 7.10).
The system shall create in-app notifications for: new request, request accepted/rejected, pickup scheduled, collection confirmed, NGO verification result.
Key notifications (OTP, verification result, password reset) shall also be sent by e-mail via SMTP.
Users shall be able to view unread notifications and mark them as read.
For a given requirement the engine shall return donations ranked by MatchScore in descending order.
Hard filters: same category; status AVAILABLE or PARTIALLY_ALLOCATED; available_quantity > 0; not deleted; not expired; distance ≤ d_max (default 50 km) unless the NGO explicitly widens the radius.
The score shall be computed with the weighted formula in Section 6.3 using configurable weights that sum to 1.0.
Each result shall show distance (km), available quantity vs remaining need, item-match level, score and an explanation ("2.1 km away, covers 100% of need").
Results shall be displayed as ranked cards and as markers on a Leaflet map with the NGO location and radius circle.
The engine shall respond within 250 ms for 100,000 active donations within the search radius (spatial index required).
All business logic, validation, authentication, authorisation, session/cookie handling, encryption, matching, file handling and logging shall be implemented in PHP on the server.
PHP code shall be structured into Controllers, Services, Repositories, Middleware and Core classes (Section 3.8); no SQL shall appear outside Repositories.
PHP errors shall be logged (Monolog) and never displayed to clients (display_errors = Off in production).
Configuration shall be read from environment variables loaded with phpdotenv.
All INSERT, SELECT, UPDATE and DELETE statements shall use PDO prepared statements with bound parameters.
Multi-step operations (allocation, cancellation, OTP redemption) shall run inside a transaction and roll back on any failure.
Foreign keys, NOT NULL, UNIQUE and CHECK constraints shall enforce integrity independently of application code.
List endpoints shall support pagination and shall never return unbounded result sets.
Delete operations on donations shall be soft deletes so historical allocations and logs remain consistent.
A session shall be created on successful login and shall store user_id, role, ngo_id (if any), csrf_token, login_time and last_activity.
The session ID shall be regenerated at login and after any privilege change.
An idle timeout of 30 minutes and an absolute lifetime of 8 hours shall be enforced server-side; expired sessions return 401 and are logged as SESSION_EXPIRED.
Logout shall clear $_SESSION, delete the session cookie and call session_destroy().
Session configuration shall use only cookies (use_only_cookies=1), strict mode (use_strict_mode=1) and disallow the session ID in URLs.
GET /api/v1/auth/me shall return the current user so the SPA can restore its state after a page refresh.
Optionally the session store shall be moved from files to PostgreSQL or Redis for multi-server deployments.
The preference cookie ss_pref shall be set when the user changes a filter, radius, view or theme, and read on the next visit to pre-populate the UI.
Cookie values shall be treated as untrusted input: the server and client shall validate the JSON schema, allowed keys and value ranges and ignore invalid cookies.
Cookies shall be set with the setcookie() options array (expires, path, secure, httponly, samesite) and never contain passwords, tokens, roles or personal data.
A cookie notice shall inform users that essential and preference cookies are used; users can clear preferences from their profile (cookie deleted by setting an expired date).
Each endpoint shall accept only its designated HTTP method(s); any other method shall return 405 Method Not Allowed with an Allow header.
GET requests shall never modify data; state-changing operations shall use POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE.
State-changing requests shall carry a CSRF token in the X-CSRF-Token header, verified against the session token with hash_equals().
For non-JS fallbacks (plain HTML forms), the hidden field _method may be used to tunnel PUT/PATCH/DELETE through POST.

Business logic shall be organised in reusable PHP methods/functions (e.g. DonationService::create(), MatchingService::rank(), CryptoService::encrypt(), Validator::validate()), each with typed parameters and return types.
The system shall encrypt donor/NGO phone numbers and donation pickup addresses with AES-256-GCM before storing them, and decrypt them only when an authorised user needs them.
A unique random IV shall be used for every encryption; decryption shall fail safely if the authentication tag does not verify.
The encryption key shall be loaded from the environment, shall be 32 bytes, and shall never be hard-coded or logged; a key_version column supports rotation.
Passwords shall be hashed (FR-AUTH-03) and shall never be encrypted reversibly.
All traffic shall use HTTPS in production.
Every API endpoint shall validate all input (body, query, path, headers, cookies, files) on the server before processing.
Validation failure shall return HTTP 422 with a JSON object listing errors per field; no partial processing shall occur.
Inputs shall be normalised (trim, Unicode normalisation) and validated by whitelist (type, length, format, range) rather than blacklist.
Output rendered in HTML shall be escaped (React escapes by default; PHP uses htmlspecialchars with ENT_QUOTES for any HTML/e-mail output).
Client-side validation shall mirror server rules but shall never be relied on.
The middleware chain shall be: authenticate → authorise role → authorise ownership → controller; failure at any step aborts the request (401 or 403).
Ownership shall be verified in SQL (e.g. WHERE id = :id AND donor_id = :uid) so that other users’ records cannot be read or modified by guessing IDs.
Failed authorisation attempts shall be logged as ACCESS_DENIED events.
There shall be no default administrator credentials; the first admin is created by a CLI seed script that prompts for the password.
Donors shall upload one or more images when adding or editing a donation; the UI shall show a preview and progress.
NGOs shall upload registration documents during registration; administrators shall be able to open them for review.
The server shall validate extension, real MIME type, size and image integrity, and shall re-encode images.
Uploaded files shall be stored outside the web root under random names and never executed.

Downloads shall be served only through GET /api/v1/media/{id}, which checks authentication and authorisation and streams the file with correct Content-Type, Content-Disposition and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff.
A "Download image" action shall be provided to authorised NGOs and donors (Content-Disposition: attachment); inline display uses inline disposition.
Filesystem paths shall never be exposed to clients; path traversal attempts shall be rejected.
Replacing or deleting a donation shall delete the associated files from storage.
The system shall write a session_logs record for every event in the table above, containing user_id (nullable), session_id (hashed), action, ip_address, user_agent, JSONB details and created_at.
At minimum, login and logout shall record login_time and logout_time (derivable from LOGIN/LOGOUT rows) and the session duration.
Log records shall be append-only: the application database role shall have INSERT and SELECT only on session_logs; UPDATE/DELETE are performed only by the retention job under a separate role.
Administrators shall view logs with filters (user, action, date range, IP) and pagination, and export the filtered result as CSV.
Every user shall be able to see their last 20 sign-ins (time, IP, browser) on the profile page.
Logs shall never contain passwords, OTPs, tokens, full session IDs or decrypted personal data; the session ID stored is a SHA-256 hash.
Log records older than 180 days shall be purged by a scheduled job.

Matching query ≤ 250 ms for 100,000 active donations within a 50 km radius (spatial index in use).
95% of API read requests ≤ 300 ms and page interactive ≤ 3 s on a 4G connection for the demo dataset.
Allocation transaction completes ≤ 100 ms under normal load.
HTTPS enforced; HSTS; secure cookies; OWASP Top 10 mitigations per Section 12.
No secrets in source control; least-privilege database roles (app role cannot alter schema or delete logs).
Critical workflows (allocation, cancellation, OTP redemption) are ACID; failure rolls back completely.
Unhandled errors return a generic 500 payload; details are written only to the server log.
Target 99% availability during the demonstration/evaluation period; daily database backup.
A new donor can publish a donation in ≤ 3 minutes without help; consistent labels and error messages.
WCAG 2.1 AA for main flows; Lighthouse accessibility score ≥ 90.
Works on the latest two versions of Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari and on Android/iOS browsers.
Layered code, PSR-12/ESLint standards, unit-test coverage ≥ 60% for services, documented API collection.
Stateless API workers; sessions and uploads can move to Redis/object storage without code change to controllers.
Runs on Windows (XAMPP), Linux and Docker with configuration through environment variables only.
All authentication and key activity events are stored in session_logs (Section 7.10).
UTF-8 everywhere; texts kept in a resource file to allow later translation; dates shown in the user’s locale.
Rate limiting shall apply to login, password reset, OTP verification and upload endpoints (HTTP 429).
The database account used by PHP shall not be a superuser and shall have only the privileges required.
Error responses shall not disclose stack traces, SQL or file paths.
Dependencies shall be audited (composer audit, npm audit) before each release.
Sensitive administrative actions shall require re-entry of the administrator’s password.

A user can register and log in; the correct role dashboard is shown. (Verification: TC-01, TC-02)
No password is stored in plaintext; hashes start with $argon2id$ or $2y$. (Verification: DB inspection)
A session is created at login with a new ID and destroyed at logout; the old session ID is invalid afterwards. (Verification: TC-03)
The ss_pref cookie is created with the specified attributes and restores the last filter after re-login; tampered values are ignored. (Verification: TC-04)
A donor can add, view, update and delete a donation. (Verification: TC-05)
An NGO can add, view, update and cancel a requirement. (Verification: TC-06)
Requests support partial quantities and cannot exceed availability. (Verification: TC-07)
With available = 5 and two pending requests of 3, concurrent accepts result in one success (available = 2) and one HTTP 409. (Verification: TC-08)
Unauthorised operations (wrong role, other user’s object) return 401/403/404. (Verification: TC-09)
Invalid input sent directly to the API (bypassing the UI) returns 422 with field errors. (Verification: TC-10)
A valid image uploads successfully and is stored under a random name outside the web root. (Verification: TC-11)
An authorised user can view/download the image; an unauthorised user receives 403. (Verification: TC-12)
The phone number column in the database is unreadable ciphertext; the app shows plaintext only to authorised users. (Verification: TC-13)
LOGIN, LOGOUT and key activity events appear in session_logs with IP and user agent, and cannot be modified via the application. (Verification: TC-14)
For an NGO at (18.5204, 73.8567), an item 2.1 km away ranks above an otherwise equal item 15.4 km away; wrong-category items never appear. (Verification: TC-15)
An administrator can verify NGOs, manage users and categories, and export logs. (Verification: TC-16)
Request and donation statuses follow the defined lifecycle; illegal transitions return 409. (Verification: TC-17)
An unverified NGO cannot create requirements or requests (403). (Verification: TC-18)
After 5 failed logins the account/IP is locked for 15 minutes (429). (Verification: TC-19)
A request cannot move from PICKUP_SCHEDULED to COLLECTED without the correct OTP; 5 wrong attempts lock the OTP. (Verification: TC-20)
A state-changing request without a valid CSRF token is rejected (403). (Verification: TC-21)
Uploading payload.php renamed to payload.png is rejected (422), and a MALICIOUS_UPLOAD_ATTEMPT event is logged. (Verification: TC-22)
A session idle for more than 30 minutes is rejected with 401 and SESSION_EXPIRED is logged. (Verification: TC-23)
SQL-injection and script payloads in text fields do not alter the database and are rendered as harmless text. (Verification: TC-24)
